decisions.title: Who invited that baby?
decisions.situation: There is a baby in the mirror. They copy every move you make. You have concerns about their manners.

result.title: Extremely rude guest
result.body: They pull it right back. You laugh and try another one.

journal.text: I made faces at my reflection and laughed when it copied me.

decisions.title: Ready for your close-up
decisions.situation: Léa points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

choices.label: Move right up to the lens
Wave at the small person on screen
Turn around at the crucial moment

result.title: Mostly nostril
result.body: Léa keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

journal.text: I gave Léa a very close view of my nose.

decisions.title: Heavy traffic
decisions.situation: A caterpillar is crossing a path. It has a lot of feet and very little urgency.

result.title: Eventually, the other side
result.body: It reaches the edge and disappears under a leaf. You remain impressed by all the feet.

journal.text: I watched a caterpillar cross a path.

decisions.title: Urgent correspondence
decisions.situation: You draw a letter and slide it into a cardboard box. It comes straight out of the missing bottom. The postal service is extremely fast.

choices.label: Fold a bottom for the box
Make a pile for each colour

result.title: Delivery delayed
result.body: The letter stays inside this time. You open the box to make sure it arrived.

journal.text: I repaired my cardboard postbox so letters would stay inside.

decisions.title: Unlimited dragons, limited shelf space
decisions.situation: At the library, you find a book so big you need both arms to carry it. The return desk suddenly looks very far away.

choices.label: Find a smaller story you love
Ask the librarian for a recommendation

result.title: An ambitious loan
result.body: You finish some of it, skip a confusing chapter, and learn three words you immediately misuse.

journal.text: I borrowed the largest book I could carry.

decisions.title: The staffroom boss fight
decisions.situation: You copied your school map from a video game. Gabriel wants to know why the staffroom is labelled “FINAL BOSS” and the toilets contain treasure.

choices.label: Replace the monsters with actual rooms
Ask whether the staffroom really is off limits
Insist the treasure is in the toilets

result.title: A less dangerous school
result.body: You redraw the map. The dragon becomes the library. Gabriel marks the corrected version and circles the one staircase you accidentally kept.

journal.text: I replaced a video-game map with a real map of my school.

decisions.title: An impressive illegal start
decisions.situation: You start a practice race before Gabriel blows the whistle. You are winning by an enormous amount.

choices.label: Laugh and wait for the next race

result.title: Same starting line
result.body: You run again with everyone else. It is harder when they are moving too.

journal.text: I restarted a practice race after jumping the whistle.

decisions.title: The homework needs rinsing
decisions.situation: Your homework went through the wash. Gabriel is holding a damp piece of paper that now says almost nothing.

choices.label: Explain and show what you remember
Claim it is an art project

result.title: Second attempt
result.body: You repeat the work and hand it in. This version stays dry.

journal.text: I redid homework that went through the wash.

decisions.title: The handle is no longer involved
decisions.situation: You knock Léa’s favourite mug off the table. The handle leaves the rest of the mug. Nobody saw.

choices.label: Slide the evidence behind a plant

result.title: Bad news, delivered properly
result.body: Léa is disappointed about the mug and pleased you said something.

journal.text: I admitted breaking Léa’s mug.

decisions.title: Your parent knows this level
decisions.situation: You promise Léa one last round. They sit down, watch your first attempt and say, “I used to beat this blindfolded.” This is an outrageous development.

choices.label: Agree on one round each, then stop

result.title: Dignity preserved
result.body: You keep your promise and turn it off. Léa seems more pleased about that than any old high score.

journal.text: I stopped a game when I had promised Léa I would.

decisions.title: The microphone is still on
decisions.situation: After a class announcement, Chloé Bernard (classmate) whispers that the school jingle sounds like a microwave. The microphone is still on.

choices.label: Switch it off and warn them

result.title: Broadcast ends
result.body: Most people heard the first comment. You prevent a second one.

journal.text: I switched off a live microphone before Chloé Bernard (classmate) said anything worse.

decisions.title: A complaint from past you
decisions.situation: You find a childhood letter addressed to yourself. It says, “If you are not a dinosaur by thirteen, you have ruined everything.” There is a drawing of the expected dinosaur.

choices.label: Make a tail out of socks and deliver a roar
Write a formal rejection on the back

result.title: Partial compliance
result.body: The tail falls off during your first turn. You add “technical difficulties” beneath the original demand and draw yourself with better knees.

journal.text: I answered a childhood demand to become a dinosaur by making a sock tail.

decisions.title: Forwarded with absolutely no evidence
decisions.situation: A group chat is circulating an embarrassing rumour about someone your age. The source appears to be “everyone knows”.

result.title: An inconvenient question
result.body: Nobody produces evidence. The conversation changes topic with suspicious speed.

journal.text: I challenged a rumour in a group chat.

decisions.title: The lost hand
decisions.situation: You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

choices.label: Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

decisions.title: A beautiful baby cabbage
decisions.situation: A fair organiser needs one more judge for a vegetable baby contest. Someone pushes a cabbage in a bonnet towards you. Its grower is waiting for a score and looks ready to take this personally.

choices.label: Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: Nothing to worry about
decisions.situation: At a free repair demonstration, a wind-up toy starts smoking. The volunteer explains that it is supposed to do that. The label “DO NOT WIND” drops off its base.

choices.label: Step back and let them stop it

result.title: A useful admission
result.body: The volunteer stops and explains the failed mechanism. You learn more from the mistake than from the planned demonstration.

journal.text: I asked about a warning label during a failed toy-repair demonstration.

decisions.title: Inside the chicken
decisions.situation: The festival mascot has quit. A volunteer thrusts a chicken suit at you and offers cash for one hour. The head smells of onions. Something inside it is still warm.

choices.label: Tell them you only came for the stalls
Carry the head around and ask if anyone knows it

result.title: A civilian again
result.body: The volunteer apologises and puts the chicken head on a traffic cone. A child immediately asks the cone for a photo.

journal.text: I declined an emergency shift inside a festival chicken.

decisions.title: A striking resemblance
decisions.situation: A caricaturist at a street fair in Lyon offers you a free sample portrait. A small crowd gathers. The artist turns the drawing around. It is you as an enormous angry thumb.

choices.label: Ask whether they could add a jawline
Ask for a pencil and draw the artist

result.title: The formal thumb
result.body: The artist adds a bow tie. You point out that this is not a jawline. A spectator says the resemblance is uncanny. You leave holding a thumb in evening wear.

journal.text: I asked a caricaturist to correct my portrait and received a thumb in a bow tie.

decisions.title: The door does not believe in you
decisions.situation: An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

decisions.title: The quiet place has noises
decisions.situation: You sit somewhere quiet and immediately notice a clock, a distant door and somebody clearing their throat. Apparently quiet did not mean perfectly silent.

choices.label: Let the ordinary sounds be there
Choose one steady sound to notice

result.title: Quiet enough is available
result.body: You stop checking each sound for a reason to be irritated. The place becomes restful without becoming silent.

journal.text: I accepted ordinary background sounds in a quiet moment.

decisions.title: You said that part out loud
decisions.situation: You rehearse a devastating comeback while walking. A stranger turns around just as you announce, “That is why nobody trusts your ferret.”

choices.label: Explain that you were arguing in your head
Write the useful point down privately
Pretend to be on an important phone call

result.title: No actual ferret dispute
result.body: The stranger accepts the explanation and walks on a little faster. You retire the argument before it recruits anyone else.

journal.text: I stopped an imaginary argument after saying part of it aloud.

decisions.title: You must make the most of it
decisions.situation: You feel better rested than usual and immediately begin planning enough tasks to use every available bit of energy.

choices.label: Choose a few priorities and leave room
Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending
result.body: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

decisions.title: Inner peace is on hold
decisions.situation: At a free relaxation class, the instructor tells you to release your anger. Their phone rings. They spend the next minute shouting at a printer repair company.

choices.label: Close your eyes and let them finish
Find peace on a walk outside
Offer to fix the printer problem

result.title: A guided loss of temper
result.body: You breathe slowly through an argument about toner. By the time they hang up, you are considerably calmer than the professional.

journal.text: I relaxed through my relaxation instructor’s furious printer call.

decisions.title: Your shoulders have a complaint
decisions.situation: After sitting in the same position for a while, you notice that your shoulders appear to have crept up towards your ears.

choices.label: Change your position and relax your shoulders

result.title: A different position helps
result.body: You loosen up at a comfortable pace and return to what you were doing. You had not noticed how stiff you were.

journal.text: I took a gentle movement break after sitting still.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in Lyon needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in Lyon.

decisions.title: Everyone else appears to be thriving
decisions.situation: Your feed contains a promotion, a beach, and a suspiciously tidy kitchen. Your own evening contains laundry.

choices.label: Close the app and finish one thing

result.title: One less pile
result.body: The laundry is still laundry. At least it is now folded.

journal.text: I stopped comparing my evening to everyone else’s highlights.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, you try a cracker that tastes strongly of cupboard. The demonstrator asks for a glowing testimonial while holding a camera.

choices.label: Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: a prolonged low mood and loss of interest. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs €30.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: Evidence from a previous haircut
decisions.situation: Léa sends you an old photograph. The haircut is difficult to defend. The memory attached to it is much better.

choices.label: Save a copy and label it

result.title: An unreliable defence witness
result.body: Léa remembers the day fondly, then admits thinking the haircut was a good idea. You forgive the first part.

journal.text: I heard the story behind an old photo. Léa also confessed to approving the haircut.

decisions.title: The missing letter
decisions.situation: A poster for a free public cookery class has dropped the L from “public”. The organiser cannot work out why people keep arriving with suspicious questions.

choices.label: Point out the missing letter quietly
Leave the organiser to discover it
Read the heading aloud to the queue

result.title: A little tape saves the afternoon
result.body: The organiser repairs the heading and looks at the queue with fresh concern. The class returns to soup.

journal.text: I pointed out an embarrassing typo on a cookery-class poster.

decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: Everyone here is a winner
decisions.situation: At a motivational taster session, you are asked to name your greatest achievement. The person before you says they survived eight workplace investigations. The facilitator applauds and turns to you.

choices.label: Say you got out of bed today
Ask what the investigations were about

result.title: A standing achievement
result.body: The facilitator calls this a triumph over horizontal thinking. Everyone stands to applaud. You sit down before they can invent a course about it.

journal.text: I told a motivational group that getting out of bed was my achievement.

decisions.title: Before answering immediately
decisions.situation: A mildly irritating question arrives while you are already tired. You notice the sharp reply forming before the other person has finished speaking.

choices.label: Say you need a short break

result.title: A reply with less edge
result.body: The pause gives you time to separate the question from your tiredness. You answer the thing that was actually asked.

journal.text: I paused before answering sharply when I was tired.

decisions.title: A minute without filling it
decisions.situation: You have a short wait with nothing to do. Before reaching for a distraction, you notice you have already checked the same screen three times.

result.title: The world supplies a few details
result.body: You notice a small sign and an interesting pattern of light. The wait becomes a moment rather than a gap to erase.

journal.text: I spent a short wait noticing what was around me.

decisions.title: Older than bread
decisions.situation: A birthday cake for you arrives with an extra zero among the candles. Someone asks whether you knew the person who invented bread.

choices.label: Ask for the extra candles to be removed
Keep the cake and accept your ancient status
Deliver a speech about surviving the last ice age

result.title: A breakthrough in reverse ageing
result.body: They remove the extra candles, then stand back as though they have made you younger. You thank the bakery for its medical breakthrough.

journal.text: I corrected an extra zero on my birthday cake.

decisions.title: A shortcut through the execution
decisions.situation: A museum shortcut in Lyon takes you through a medieval punishment exhibit. A mechanical executioner swings a foam axe across the marked path. The long route has no executioner.

choices.label: Time the swing and walk through slowly
Sprint straight through the swinging axe

result.title: A head start
result.body: You turn back. A speaker announces, “The coward flees!” Three visitors turn to look. You continue with your head and your dignity approximately intact.

journal.text: I took the long route around a museum’s mechanical executioner.

journal.text: I practised the basics at a free self-defence lesson.

Leave the soup to its lawyers
Publish a detailed attack on their diagram

result.title: A narrow defence
result.body: You clarify that your review concerns lunch rather than civilisation. The diagram receives no further comment.

journal.text: I clarified a soup review after a stranger took it personally.

decisions.title: The accidental millionaire
decisions.situation: At a charity auction, someone mistakes you for a wealthy donor. The auctioneer hands you the microphone beside a photograph of an elderly donkey. “How much will you give?” The room goes quiet.

choices.label: Admit your wealth has been exaggerated
Claim you are the donkey’s lawyer

result.title: A donkey-sized misunderstanding
result.body: You explain that you were looking for the toilets. The auctioneer takes back the microphone and points down the corridor. Several people applaud your honesty. One applauds the donkey.

journal.text: I admitted I was not the wealthy donor a charity auction expected.

decisions.title: One missed intention
decisions.situation: You miss a small personal intention and catch yourself declaring the whole effort ruined. The declaration is much larger than the missed step.

choices.label: Ask whether the intention needs adjusting

result.title: A smaller conclusion
result.body: You treat the missed moment as one moment and carry on with what you can manage now.

journal.text: I avoided turning a small missed intention into a verdict on everything.

decisions.title: A number with nowhere to go

choices.label: Return calmly to the original task
Treat the distraction as a personal crisis

result.title: An impressive useless recital
result.body: You repeat the number once and laugh at the timing. Memory has supplied an answer to a question nobody asked.

journal.text: I remembered an old telephone number at an unhelpful moment.
